content: Nothing is burdensome if taken lightly, and nothing need arouse your irritation so long as you don't make it irritate you.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Vita Beata (On the Happy Life)
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Seneca's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
